clue.text: Veronica will go quickly by the spring

parts.note: to speed is to go quickly
a well is a spring of water from the ground

explanation.surface: Someone called Veronica will be hurrying off as spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name but is the botanical name of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is the genus name of the small blue-flowered plant also called by this common name.

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A friend made a feeble, trifling effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something trifling or of little worth.

clue.text: Prophet or priest having a beer, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver the letters are only how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: Eli is the biblical priest, and a jar is a glass of beer, so the priest is having a jar

explanation.surface: A clergyman or holy seer settles down with a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, ELI + JAR (a jar being a pint of beer) sounds like the prophet's name. Eli was the priest who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is an Old Testament prophet who was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the letters of the words that follow are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: The war ruined the cenotaph.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers laid at a cenotaph serves as a memorial to the dead.

clue.text: Who goes first? It is not encouraged in cross-examination

definitions.text: It is not encouraged in cross-examination

explanation.surface: A query about who leads off, and a courtroom no-no.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, 'who is in front?' is an inquiry about the one ahead; in court, a prompting query suggesting its own reply is frowned upon.

clue.text: Action taken by railway worker back in front

indicators.note: in front places the word for back before the railway worker

parts.note: the rear is the back
a guard is a member of a train crew

explanation.surface: Something done by a train employee at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front' puts REAR before GUARD. The definition leans on the phrase 'rearguard action', a defensive fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a last defensive stand, so the word stands for that kind of action.

parts.note: retired suggests old, past working age
a master is the captain of a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A portrait belonging to a former ship's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Master is a painting by a great European artist from before about 1800.

parts.note: read whimsically, the crossness of someone who sets exams is the mood that belongs to testing

explanation.surface: A tetchy invigilator.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means touchiness or short temper, and its first syllables suggest a test.

parts.note: meal is coarsely ground grain
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry: the grain in question is corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealie is the southern African word for corn on the cob.

clue.text: Narrow-minded being against a political group?

explanation.surface: Prejudice against a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as ILL (hostile) towards LIBERALs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means intolerant, and whimsically it is being ill-disposed to the Liberal party.

explanation.surface: Standing by to help a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means quick and on time, and also to feed a forgotten line to someone on stage.

clue.text: Ban priest who is breaking an ornamental clip

indicators.note: breaking signals that the two words before it are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Bar the cleric who is damaging a decorative brooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges BAN PRIEST; 'who is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastpin is a brooch worn on the chest, a decorative clasp.

indicators.note: uproariously suggests the dogs' noise, so the letters of the dog word are thrown about

explanation.surface: Dogs howl noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a verb for hounds howling, but it is a noun: the Canadian Hudson Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay is the huge inlet in north-eastern Canada.

explanation.surface: A stand-in for a performer without work.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare component replaces a broken one; whimsically, an actor not cast in any role.

clue.text: A harvest on soil cultivated in Greece

parts.note: a crop is a harvest

indicators.note: cultivated means the earth word is worked over, its letters turned

explanation.surface: A farmer's yield grown on Greek earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' turns SOIL into OLIS. The definition names a landmark found in Greece, chiefly in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the ancient citadel standing above Athens.

clue.text: Inclination and ability or self control

parts.note: will is wish or inclination
power is capacity or ability

explanation.surface: A list of virtues: desire, capability, restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength of will is the discipline to resist temptation.

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone, for example, owns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the definition: the self.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' of psychology.

indicators.note: consumed by says the food is eaten up inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tramp eats a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen's egg is a common food.

explanation.surface: Sacked for walking off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman dismissed in cricket is out, and striking workers are out.

parts.note: scraps reads as leftovers, but as fights, choosing them is starting arguments on purpose

explanation.surface: Selecting leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick a fight is to provoke one; scraps are fights, so selecting them means looking for trouble.

indicators.note: returning means the word for the boat is read backwards

parts.note: a tug is a small powerful boat

explanation.surface: A vessel heading back across the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel, but the definition is a narrow passage of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut is a narrow strait or water passage.

clue.text: Grub for Australian animal let out

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo

indicators.note: out here means the word let is thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Food for a kangaroo that has been released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into TLE. 'Grub' looks like food, but it is a verb: to rummage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rootle is to dig or rummage about, as a pig grubs for food.

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps, with the possessive S
cue is how the letter Q is spelt out

explanation.surface: Get back a mechanic's note.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue something is to save or retrieve it.

clue.text: Silk fabric worn by small number in dance one leaves at the end

indicators.note: in places the small number inside what remains of the dance
leaves at the end says the word for one departs from the tail of the dance

parts.note: a veleta is an old-time ballroom dance
a, the indefinite article, means one
V is the Roman numeral five, a small number

explanation.surface: A dress of fine cloth worn at a ball that someone leaves late.
explanation.walkthrough: A VELETA is a British old-time sequence dance. 'leaves at the end' drops its final A, giving VELET, and V goes 'in'; 'worn by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a soft, thick-piled fabric traditionally woven from silk.

parts.note: read as fasting too much rather than going too quickly, this means going hungry

explanation.surface: Excessive speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting to excess means going without food until near death.

clue.text: She could take you in for screening

definitions.text: She could take you in for screening

parts.words: She could take you in for screening
parts.note: screening suggests a medical check, but here it is a film showing and taking in means guiding to a seat

explanation.surface: A nurse leading a patient for a medical test.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema attendant who shows patrons to their seats for a film.

clue.text: In favour of not returning for a bit

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: returning means the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporting the idea of not coming back for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a subatomic particle, a tiny bit of an atom.

clue.text: The finding of a famous ship

explanation.surface: Locating a celebrated vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a find; it is also Captain Scott's Antarctic expedition vessel, now at Dundee.

explanation.surface: Broke and fallen down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means financially wrecked, and also fallen into decay like an old castle.

clue.text: Restless when the bills have not been paid?

definitions.text: when the bills have not been paid?

explanation.surface: Uneasy while debts are outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means agitated, and also describes accounts still owed.
